annotations.note: Synge's 1966 paper on photon escape from compact stars is the classic derivation of the escape cone set by the photon sphere, i.e. the shadow boundary; only its abstract was available, and the off-topic tag (both pipelines) is wrong.
Joint citation [12, 13]: Virbhadra & Ellis define the Schwarzschild photon sphere at r = 3M (the circular photon orbits); the shadow part is carried by Synge [12].

Claudel, Virbhadra and Ellis introduced the (quasi-local) definition of photon surfaces, which the field credits as the first; the paper not saying 'first' about itself does not make the attribution wrong.
The correspondence F = f, H = 1/g matches the cited metric; the remark about a sign difference from metric signature is the citing authors' own comparison.
Claudel et al. give the unit normal of an SO(3)-invariant timelike hypersurface in a general spherically symmetric metric; the citing authors write it in their own f, g notation.
The citation points to the conserved-orbital-angular-momentum method of [45]; applying it to general timelike circular orbits is the citing authors' own step.
As for s28: the general unit-normal formula of [32], specialised by the citing authors to Vaidya coordinates.
'Consistent with the result in [45]': [45] obtains the ISCO evolution in Vaidya spacetime (numerically, shown in a figure); the consistency check is the citing authors'.

Cederbaum & Jahns treat spherical photon orbits (constant r) in Kerr; extending 'not evolved, r = constant' to general stationary axisymmetric spacetimes goes a little beyond the source. The corrected-source tag (an erratum) is legitimate.
The cited work gives the slow-rotation Kerr-Vaidya metric on the equatorial plane, which is what the marker is attached to; the tangent-vector definitions that follow are the citing authors'.

'The result is consistent with [45]': [45] derives ISCO evolution equations in dynamical spherically symmetric spacetimes by another method; the consistency is the citing authors' own comparison (both pipelines too literal).
